notes: Poses can now be done the simple way, and the parts that had piled up around the hard way are gone. The simple way is what Grok does: show a model her pictures and the pose picture and say "her, in that". No skeleton, no depth map, no LoRA for the pose, and a foot pointed at the camera is just a foot the model can see. It runs on your own GPU, on Qwen-Image-Edit, which takes three pictures at once and moderates nothing; identity comes from the reference pictures on her card, and her face LoRA still gets its turn afterwards in the face pass on FLUX, which is the pairing that works best. Every pose in the library now has a choice, Reference or Skeleton, with Auto following a default under Your own GPU; a picture is usable as a reference the moment it is added, and Extract is only for the skeleton way, which stays for when nothing of the reference person should come through. The Photo Lab has the same choice, a one-off picture option, and shows her references beside the pose so you can see what the model will be shown. Install edit model puts the three files (about 30GB, once) on the volume, and Check edit model under Diagnostics confirms the worker knows the nodes; if a reference edit fails, the photo falls back to the skeleton route on its own. Gone: the Kontext subject-swap and its stitched pair, the Lab's picture-repaint row with its denoise slider, and their install, check and settings copy. The Kontext files on the volume are not touched; they can be deleted to make room.
